consumer: The fetch task's 'objective met' indicator, which asks: has the engine's objective/mission completion predicate determined the required parts are now accounted for?
scope: The full reachable inventory the fetch objective counts over (player inventory plus worn/wielded items and reachable/nearby containers), matching the objective's own counting reach rather than only loose ground-item stacks on nearby tiles.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_entities(items) iterates points_in_radius and emits only get_map().i_at(p) ground stacks per tile (charges, count_by_charges) into entities.items[]; it reports raw map ground items and never the objective's computed completion value.
divergence: The required part sits in the player's backpack (or a worn/wielded slot, or inside a closed crate) rather than loose on a nearby tile: the engine objective is met and the indicator would light, but map::i_at returns no such item on any tile, so this surface reports the objective unmet (false negative the engine's own predicate would not produce).
